content.Text: I’m trying a variant that uses actual rebinding of a captured global cell, not just array mutation, because that tends to be the highest-value source of mistakes. I’ll keep only the version whose semantics stay crisp and fully deterministic.

class Cell:
    def __init__(self,v): self.v=v
outs=[]
def pr(x): outs.append(x)

x=Cell([2,1])

def maker(a_val):
    a=Cell(a_val)
    b=Cell([a.v[1], a.v[0]])
    def f1(d_val):
        d=Cell(d_val)
        a.v[0]=a.v[0]+d.v
        b.v=[b.v[0]+a.v[0], a.v[1]+d.v]
        x.v=[x.v[1]+b.v[0], x.v[0]+a.v[0]]
        def f2(k_val):
            k=Cell(k_val)
            a_shadow=Cell([b.v[1], k.v])
            x.v[0]=x.v[0]+a_shadow.v[0]
            b.v[1]=b.v[1]+x.v[1]
            return x.v[0]+x.v[1]+b.v[0]+b.v[1]+a_shadow.v[0]+a_shadow.v[1]
        return f2
    return f1

f=maker(x.v)
g=f(2)
pr(sum(x.v))
h=f(1)
pr(g(3))
pr(h(0))
pr(sum(x.v))
y=[3,4]
p=maker(y)
q=p(2)
pr(q(1))
pr(sum(y))
pr(g(0))
pr(sum(x.v))
print(outs)
